key_insight: A hybrid CNN-cellular automata model is used to plan aerial wildfire suppression by jointly predicting fire spread and optimizing targeted drop actions.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps operational planners choose where and how to deploy water or retardant drops to reduce burned area under uncertainty.
method: Predicts wildfire spread from terrain, fuel, and wind using a hybrid neural-cellular automaton model.
Optimizes binary aerial drop decisions with continuous location and orientation parameters mapped to the simulation grid.
Models water and retardant separately, including immediate burn reduction and longer-lasting suppression effects.
evidence_signal: A case study on the 2020 Bear Fire evaluates suppression schedules and uncertainty using Monte Carlo fire-state sampling plus spatially correlated prediction-error perturbations.
watch_item: Results depend on the fidelity of the fire model and uncertainty assumptions, so real-world deployment will require careful calibration and operational validation.
paper_title: Aerial Wildfire Suppression Planning with a Hybrid CNN-Cellular Automata Fire Model
